body.x: VietnamPlus, Vietnam's state-run digital news portal, named Farmity Co., Ltd., JINMYUNG I&C Co., Ltd. and iM Robotics its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

VietnamPlus is the official digital news portal operated by Vietnam's state news agency. It has covered technology, innovation, digital transformation, AI, advanced technologies, startups and the digital economy, and publishes in five languages: Vietnamese, English, French, Chinese and Russian. With about 30 million page views a month and a range of social media channels, it connects readers in Vietnam and abroad with the industry ecosystem.

VietnamPlus returned as a FIX global media partner for FIX 2026, two years after FIX 2024. In a pre-event interview, Võ Hoàng Long, a reporter and deputy editor-in-chief at the outlet, said he would focus on how AI is converging with robotics, mobility and manufacturing, and on whether the technology is moving beyond demonstrations toward commercialization and use at actual sites. He also said he hoped to examine Korean companies' AI, robotics and smart manufacturing technology and to find solutions that fit Vietnam's industrial environment and openings for cooperation between companies in the two countries.

The three companies VietnamPlus picked are Farmity, a spatial intelligence company that uses mmWave radar and vision AI; JINMYUNG I&C, which provides AI video surveillance and integrated broadcasting and audio solutions; and iM Robotics, which develops indoor and outdoor autonomous mobile robots (AMRs). They work in different fields: spatial awareness and safety management, intelligent surveillance and autonomous logistics. Together, they show how AI and automation technology can be applied at industrial sites.
Farmity Applies Radar and Vision Spatial AI to 3D Awareness and Safety

Farmity Co., Ltd. develops spatial intelligence (spatial AI) solutions that analyze movement and conditions in a space using radar and video recognition. Its main technology families are FIRA, based on mmWave radar, and FIVIS, based on video analysis. Using different sensing methods, they recognize and analyze people's postures and movements and hazards in a space.

FIRA Pose, in the FIRA series, uses AI to analyze mmWave radar signals and estimate a person's 3D posture and movement. Because it detects body posture and behavior without relying on camera images, it offsets limits of video-based recognition such as lighting and occlusion, and helps reduce the privacy concerns that come with filming. Building on its ability to detect specific behavior patterns such as falls, the company is exploring uses in hospital rooms, smart homes and industrial sites. FIRA Vital uses mmWave radar to measure biometric information such as heart rate and breathing without contact and to monitor a person's condition.

FIVIS, the video-based family, infers depth information from existing camera footage and converts it into 3D spatial information to analyze people's movement and hazards. The industrial safety solution FIVIS SafeX is designed to use existing CCTV infrastructure to detect workers' behavior and posture, entry into danger zones, and abnormal situations such as fire and intrusion, and to connect with control systems. Farmity is also widening its range of applications with products such as FIVIS MediX, which supports 3D analysis of medical images.

In industrial safety management, contactless monitoring in medical settings and intelligent control of public facilities, technology that understands the location, posture and behavior of people and objects, not just whether they are present, is becoming more important. Farmity develops spatial intelligence technology on two different recognition methods, radar and vision, aiming for AI that grasps conditions in real spaces and supports response on site.
JINMYUNG I&C Links AI CCTV and Integrated Broadcasting and Audio Technology for Site Safety

JINMYUNG I&C Co., Ltd. is an ICT company that develops and supplies broadcasting, audio and video surveillance systems. Its offerings include in-house broadcasting equipment, video surveillance equipment and security cameras, along with AI-based object detection, intelligent video analytics, fire detection and integrated control solutions.

AI CCTV goes beyond recording and storing video: it analyzes objects and situations in footage to identify specific behavior or signs of trouble. The company's intelligent camera lineup includes AI-based object detection and video analytics, and its video surveillance systems can support security and safety management at public facilities and industrial sites. By handling broadcasting and audio systems together with video surveillance, it supplies the range of ICT equipment needed for site operations.

Broadcasting and audio systems are used for announcements and emergency messages at public facilities and workplaces, and linked with video surveillance they can form an integrated environment for understanding conditions on site and delivering the information needed. JINMYUNG I&C has strengthened its technology through designations for its in-house broadcasting and video surveillance equipment as an excellent product and a quality-assured item by Korea's government procurement agency, as well as through patents and various certifications.

AI-based video analytics and integrated control technology help facility managers grasp conditions across large spaces efficiently and respond to hazards such as fire or intrusion. With solutions that combine video surveillance with broadcasting and audio technology, JINMYUNG I&C supports security, safety management and information delivery at public and industrial sites.
iM Robotics Builds Indoor and Outdoor AMRs for Logistics and Industrial Automation

iM Robotics develops and manufactures autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that move and carry materials and goods at logistics and industrial sites. The company has indoor and outdoor lineups and offers a range of models so customers can configure a mobility solution to site conditions and load requirements.

The indoor lineup includes the M200-I, M300-I, M1000-I and M2000-I. Load capacity, size and driving performance vary by model, so customers can choose according to the work environment and what they carry. The outdoor lineup includes the M500-OC and M500-OW, designed for outdoor travel and special-purpose work. Some models can be configured with top modules or special-purpose equipment such as lifts, conveyors and collaborative robots to suit the application.

Because an AMR can carry materials along a route inside a workplace without relying on fixed conveyor lines, it helps make logistics flow more flexible. At manufacturing and logistics sites, mobile robots that automate transfers between processes and repetitive hauling, and that adapt to changes in the work environment, are becoming more important.

iM Robotics responds to demand for logistics automation at industrial sites with AMR lineups for indoor and outdoor environments and customized mobility solutions. Robots that move through a workspace carrying goods can raise the efficiency of manufacturing and logistics operations, and can later be linked with other automation equipment to build smart manufacturing environments.
Finding Applications in Vietnam's Industrial Sector

VietnamPlus's top three span three technology fields: spatial intelligence AI, intelligent video surveillance and autonomous mobile robots. Farmity uses radar and video data to recognize the conditions of people and spaces, JINMYUNG I&C supports on-site monitoring and information delivery with AI CCTV and broadcasting and audio systems, and iM Robotics supports transport and carrying at logistics and industrial sites with indoor and outdoor autonomous robots.

What the three have in common is that their technology moves past analyzing data and connects to work on site, detecting hazards or moving goods. Safety management, video surveillance and logistics automation are key tasks in manufacturing's digital transformation, and demand from companies that want to apply spatial recognition and automation technology on site is expected to keep growing.

In its FIX 2026 pre-event interview, VietnamPlus said it wanted to see how Korean AI, robotics and smart manufacturing technology is applied in real business and to find solutions and cooperation opportunities suited to Vietnam's industrial environment. From that viewpoint, the three companies can be introduced as cases of applying technology to specific problems on site, such as industrial safety, intelligent surveillance and logistics automation.

The Global Media Awards let media from each country find Korean companies from the standpoint of their own specialty and market and introduce them to overseas readers. The selection is expected to widen contact between Vietnam's market, which is pursuing digital transformation and smart manufacturing, and Korean technology companies, and to open the way to business cooperation and technology exchange.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including VietnamPlus. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet covering IT, enterprise digital transformation (DX) and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.Net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners took part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and covered firsthand news from innovative companies set to lead Korea's future industries, introducing it to readers around the world.
